additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
concerning Volvo OAL-VM 69 we used our D300 Sicharges today in the morning at our branch in Pentling and during lunch at our depot. After the Volvo update on Monday the “frozen” power at SoC 80 % is history – a success for our drivers.

What you also can see:
- the car did not get it’s max. power of 250 kW (today it’s a cloudy day, appr. 10°C)
- no break / valley at SoC 80%, not for seconds or minutes
- good power up to SoC 98 % …this problem is solved
In this case we could repeat an other issue, reported in Siemens Ticket CRM 02023000385. The re-allocation of the 4 power-united could/should more intelligent … you call it highflex
J

Hi Francisco,
sorry for the circumstances concering your name.
I think it’s too late, because this morning at 8 o’clock this truck got this update. First observation of our driver was positive: at 80 % SoC a short reducing of power, after it power was increased.
We organized this update last week due to an advice of Volvo, that this bug was fixed and only on this truck it was missing.
Nevertheless we will have a closer look on VM69, if this problem is solved.
So on Thursday we have perhaps only one scenario left: missing power of D300 during one truck is loading (perhaps temperature of pins inside the css2-plug).
Viele Grüße
Martin Glöckner

Thank you for the fast reply.
When you say Francesco, I believe you are talking about me, my last names are “de Matos Joaquim”

I come requesting for the following: please do not update the Volvo truck as this is the one where we want to test. The other Volvos do not have this battery management logic, that’s why it doesn’t have any problem.
It’s up to you if you want to update the truck or not as it might disrupt operations, if you get this update, it will always give full power.
Please let us know if you updated the truck or not.
